headline: DRAM contract prices seen rising about 20% QoQ in 4Q26
quote: Fourth-quarter DRAM contract prices are expected to rise about 20% quarter-on-quarter.
claim: TrendForce News, which says it curates updates independently of TrendForce's research team, relayed a Commercial Times report on 20 Oct 2026 that fourth-quarter DRAM contract prices are expected to rise about 20% quarter-on-quarter. The report calls that a slowdown from approximately 80% in the second quarter and 40% in the third, reflecting a higher comparison base, weakening end-market purchasing power and long-term-agreement price ceilings.
why_it_matters: Memory is still getting dearer, only more slowly, which feeds into what a RAM upgrade for an old laptop or a 24 GB machine costs.
title: [News] DRAM Prices Seen Rising 20% QoQ in 4Q26 Despite Slower Gains; AI Demand, Tight Supply Support Outlook

headline: SSD contract prices reportedly up 303% in a year on NAND shortage
quote: The contract price of a 256GB TLC SSD reached approximately $134.20 in the third quarter of 2026, up from $33.30 a year earlier.
claim: Notebookcheck, citing Tech Insider, reported on 25 Oct 2026 that a 256GB TLC SSD's contract price reached about $134.20 in the third quarter of 2026, up 303% year over year and roughly 20% on the previous quarter. It stresses these are contract rather than retail prices, and says TrendForce forecasts NAND flash contract prices rising another 15% to 20% quarter over quarter in the fourth quarter of 2026.
why_it_matters: Contract prices have more than quadrupled in a year, though not every retail SSD has; new supply may not arrive until mid-to-late 2027, so bigger drives stay costly.
title: SSD prices explode by 303 % in a year as AI fuels NAND flash shortage - Notebookcheck News

headline: RTX 5090 nearly gone from US retail, custom cards from $8,500
quote: Redirected supply and aggressive grey-market recycling have nearly wiped out GeForce RTX 5090 stock from U.S. retailers.
claim: Tom's Hardware reported on 24 Oct 2026 that GeForce RTX 5090 stock has nearly vanished from US retailers and that custom cards now start at $8,500. It says a newly surfaced video shows Chinese workshops moving the GB202 GPU and GDDR7 onto dual-slot blower boards for AI servers, and that Nvidia has reportedly halted RTX 5090 production.
why_it_matters: Flagship GeForce silicon is going to AI servers, so top-end GPU prices now follow data-centre demand rather than gamers or students.
title: Leaked video exposes how industrial-scale Chinese factories are dismantling RTX 5090s by the thousands to fuel AI servers — GPU die and memory desoldered and transplanted to blower designs; custom cards to Nvidia Founders Editions on the chopping block | Tom's HardwareTom's Hardware

headline: Utho Cloud opens NVIDIA B300 reservations in India ahead of February 2027
quote: Indian cloud provider Utho Cloud has opened reservations for NVIDIA B300 GPUs in India ahead of a planned February 2027 deployment
claim: Analytics India Magazine reported on 19 Oct 2026 that Utho Cloud has opened reservations for NVIDIA B300 GPUs in India, with deployment planned for February 2027, one-to-three-year reservations, rupee-based billing and India-hosted infrastructure. The article gives no prices and no count of B300 GPUs available.
why_it_matters: Rupee-billed, India-hosted B300 capacity is on one-to-three-year reservations aimed at businesses, so it signals where Indian GPU supply is heading, not hourly rental for students.
title: Utho Cloud Opens B300 GPU Bookings Ahead of February 2027 Rollout
